claim: the minmax projection falls back to bisection's count, 21 trials for the default tolerance
fix: its minmax projection holds it at about ITP's worst case, 21 or 22 trials for the default tolerance against plain bisection's 20.
ver_evidence: probe.jl P2 (line 118): the strict-gate leaves take 21,22,22,22,22,22 trials at Δt_frame = 1//100 and 21,22,22,21,21,22 at 1//10. Plain bisection (the ±1 gate) takes 20. src/frame.jl:372 n_max = ceil(-log2(tol)) + 1 = 21 is ITP's minmax bound, not bisection's count. The totals, 177 against 87, match the doc.
ver_note: The doc's total of 177 matches exactly at Δt_frame = 1//100, so only the per-leave figure and the 'bisection's count' label are off. A leave taking 22 trials passes ITP's n_max of 21 by one, probably because the stop test is the strict hi - lo > tol.

claim: the +-1 gate converges at the same bisection count as the strict gate
fix: Writing `one(u)` instead of `-u` on the holding side defines the same predicate and converges at plain bisection's count, 20 trials, one or two fewer per leave than the strict gate, because both ends of the bracket are then fake constants.
ver_evidence: probe.jl P2: the ±1 gate takes exactly 20 trials per leave (166 total at 1//100, 167 at 1//10). The strict gate takes 21-22 per leave (177 and 176). With σlo = -1 and σhi = 1 the regula falsi point is the midpoint (src/frame.jl:377), so ±1 is pure bisection and needs one or two fewer trials than the strict gate.
